newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices expected to be firmer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices expected to be firmer.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to be generally firm, with good demand for quality fine wool types, pastoral group Wesfarmers Dalgety said.
Sales this week are in Newcastle, Melbourne and Fremantle with 106,000 bales on offer.
The eastern market indicator remained unchanged at 589 cents a kg clean last week, while the western market indicator closed six cents lower at 525 cents.
Wesfarmers said Chinese demand was expected to support the medium and broad micron wool prices again this week.
Fine wool prices would be tested by sales in Newcastle which included a majority of fine and superfine types, it said.
"An increase in European interest will be necessary to maintan this end of the market over the coming weeks of seasonally higher volumes," Wesfarmers said.

"With the political noises being made about possible trade implications of the Dalai Lama's visit to Australia, it is reassuring that the commercial interests in both China and Australia are clearly intent on maintaining the current trade in wool between the two countries," the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
